The existence of this JSON file, and any script (including scripts/bin/validate-plan.mjs) successfully validating its shape, does NOT constitute approval to apply anything. `root` below is a placeholder (`<TARGET_ROOT>`); until it is replaced with the actual target directory's absolute path, `validate-plan.mjs` returns FAIL on this file — that is intentional, not a defect. Applying any of the changes below to a real repository requires that repository's owner to explicitly approve this exact plan content, re-checked against the current state of the target files, in a separate `apply` step. `checks[].approved` is `false` in this sample for the same reason: the sample's existence is not approval.

target.description: Monorepo with a pnpm + Turborepo-managed apps/packages tree (JS/TS) and a separate Cargo workspace under rust/ producing a native addon consumed by one Node package. Root README currently lists two unrelated blocks of copy-pasted commands ('for the JS side, run X'; 'for the Rust side, run Y') and there is no single command a new contributor or CI can run to validate the whole repo.

existingEntryPoints: pnpm turbo run lint test build (JS/TS side, Turborepo owns caching + task graph)
cargo test && cargo build --release (Rust side, under rust/)
existingRunners: GitHub Actions (two separate jobs, no ordering guarantee today)

adoptedEntryPoint.role: root-level integration window only — Make owns neither Turborepo's task graph/cache nor Cargo's dependency graph
adoptedEntryPoint.rationale: Each ecosystem already has a tool that correctly owns its own dependency graph and cache (Turborepo for JS/TS, Cargo for Rust). This plan does not re-implement either. Make is adopted solely at the repository root to express the one real cross-ecosystem ordering constraint that exists today (the Node package's build consumes the compiled Rust addon) and to give both a human and CI one name (`make verify`) instead of two undocumented, unordered command blocks.

sourceOfTruth.concern: JS/TS task graph, caching, parallel execution
sourceOfTruth.notes: Unchanged; make delegates to `pnpm turbo run ...`, never re-lists individual package scripts.
Unchanged; make delegates to `cargo ...` inside rust/, never touches rust/target directly.

sourceOfTruth.concern: cross-ecosystem build order (addon must exist before the Node package that embeds it builds)
sourceOfTruth.notes: The one real gap this plan closes: today this order is only documented in prose, not enforced anywhere.

commandContract.name: help
commandContract.purpose: List public root commands and what each one delegates to.

commandContract.name: check
commandContract.purpose: Fast feedback: lint only, both ecosystems, no builds/tests.
commandContract.scope: whole repo (both ecosystems), or a single changed package via Turborepo's own filtering

entryPoints.direct: (pnpm turbo run lint) and, separately, (cd rust && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings)

commandContract.name: verify
commandContract.purpose: Full required validation for both ecosystems, in the one order that matters: Rust addon built and tested first, then the JS/TS side (which may depend on the built addon).
commandContract.sideEffects: writes to rust/target and to Turborepo's own cache directory; no source rewrites

entryPoints.direct: (cd rust && cargo test && cargo build --release) then (pnpm turbo run lint test build)

commandContract.notes: The ordering (Rust before JS/TS) is the entire reason this target exists; it is expressed as a real Make prerequisite (rust-verify before js-verify below), not as two independently-run README steps a human might reorder by mistake.

commandContract.name: fix
commandContract.purpose: Auto-fix formatting/lint issues Turborepo and Cargo each already know how to fix.
commandContract.sideEffects: rewrites source files in place in both ecosystems

entryPoints.direct: (pnpm turbo run fix) and (cd rust && cargo fmt)

commandContract.name: clean
commandContract.purpose: Remove each ecosystem's own regenerable build output via that ecosystem's own clean command.
commandContract.sideEffects: deletes rust/target and Turborepo/pnpm's own cache and dist output (both are regenerable; nothing under src trees is touched)

entryPoints.direct: (cd rust && cargo clean) and (pnpm turbo run clean, or rm -rf per-package dist/ if no such script exists)

changes.description: Root-level thin Makefile. `verify` target has a REAL prerequisite edge from a `rust-verify` phony target to a `js-verify` phony target (not sibling prerequisites on one line), so `make -j` cannot start the JS/TS side before the Rust addon exists. `check`/`fix`/`clean` remain unordered (both sides are independent for those).

Replace the two separate 'for the JS side' / 'for the Rust side' command blocks with `make help` at the top, keeping each ecosystem's direct commands as the documented fallback immediately below (per this Skill's requirement that Make stays optional).

Replace the two independent, unordered jobs with a single job calling `make verify`, so CI enforces the same Rust-before-JS ordering the Makefile now expresses, instead of relying on two jobs that happen to both pass independently of order.

keepExisting: turbo.json task graph, pipeline definitions, and remote/local cache configuration are entirely unchanged.
rust/Cargo.toml workspace layout, members, and feature flags are entirely unchanged.
pnpm-lock.yaml and pnpm as the package manager are unchanged; this plan does not introduce or evaluate a different package manager.

addedDependencies.name: GNU Make
addedDependencies.kind: build-time tool, developer machine + CI runner
addedDependencies.reason: Required only to use the new root `make <target>` convenience entry points; every target has a documented direct fallback (turbo / cargo commands) so neither building the addon, running the JS/TS side, nor contributing to either package requires Make to be installed.
addedDependencies.alreadyPresent: assumed present on CI's ubuntu-latest image; not assumed present on every contributor machine, hence the retained direct-command fallback in README.

risks.description: Serializing rust-verify before js-verify removes today's (accidental) job-level parallelism in CI, since the two GitHub Actions jobs currently run concurrently on separate runners.
risks.mitigation: CI wall-clock time may increase; if that becomes a problem, keep the two CI jobs separate but add an explicit `needs:` edge between them at the CI-orchestrator layer instead of merging into one `make verify` job — same ordering guarantee, restores runner-level parallelism with other unrelated jobs. This plan does not decide that trade-off; it is called out here as a documented open question for whoever approves this plan.

risks.description: The rust/target and Turborepo cache directories are currently namespaced per-worktree by convention (not enforced); a root Makefile invoked from two Git worktrees of this repo at once could still collide on either cache if a contributor points both worktrees at a shared cache path.
risks.mitigation: Not addressed by this plan (out of scope); flagged for the target repo's own worktree-isolation practice, per this Skill's operations/parallelism-and-recovery.md guidance.

alternatives.name: No root Makefile; document the required order in README prose only
alternatives.description: Keep today's two command blocks but add a sentence saying 'run the Rust block first'.
alternatives.whyNotChosen: Already tried (implicitly) today via block ordering in the README and it does not prevent a contributor or a future CI edit from running the two independently; a real dependency edge in a Makefile is enforced, prose is not.

alternatives.name: Move the ordering into Turborepo itself (a turbo.json task depending on a script that shells out to cargo)
alternatives.description: Model the Rust build as a Turborepo task with its own dependsOn edge to the JS build task.
alternatives.whyNotChosen: Would make Turborepo responsible for orchestrating a non-JS toolchain it has no native awareness of (cache invalidation on Rust source changes would need to be hand-modeled as extra turbo.json inputs); the thin root Makefile expresses the one cross-ecosystem edge without asking either tool to model the other's internals. Reconsider if more than this single cross-ecosystem edge accumulates.

migrationSteps.action: Add root Makefile with rust-verify and js-verify as separate phony targets, each delegating verbatim to today's existing direct commands (no behavior change yet).

Add `verify: rust-verify js-verify` (in this order) as a real prerequisite list, and confirm `make -j2 verify` still runs rust-verify to completion before js-verify starts (Make serializes true prerequisite chains regardless of -j).
Update README to lead with `make help`, retaining both ecosystems' direct commands beneath it.

Update .github/workflows/ci.yml to a single job calling `make verify`; explicitly note in the same PR the CI-parallelism trade-off from the risks section above, so reviewers can decide whether to keep the two-job/needs: alternative instead.

staticOnly: Confirm no existing root Makefile already exists at the target root (this plan assumes creation, not replacement).
Confirm turbo.json's existing task names (lint/test/build/fix/clean) actually match the ones this plan's Makefile delegates to; do not assume Turborepo task names without reading turbo.json first.
verificationPlan.note: The executable verification commands themselves are the machine-readable `checks` array at the top level of this plan (not duplicated here); see `checks[].name == "verify"` and `checks[].name == "rust-verify"`.

approval.approvalMechanism: Explicit user sign-off on this plan's filesToChange list and on the CI-parallelism trade-off noted under risks, given after re-reading the target files' current state at apply time.
